This semester my M.Sc. Data Science students at MSE had an extra teaching assistant for two courses, Statistics with R and Introduction to Artificial Intelligence. It never slept, never lost patience, and answered only from my course notes. Here is how it came together.

## Why bother

Doubts don't keep office hours. They turn up at 1 a.m., the night before an exam. A general-purpose chatbot will answer at that hour too, but in its own notation, with its own examples, and sometimes with confident nonsense. I wanted answers that matched what we had done in class.

## Starting small

I had considered building a custom system. I started instead with a free, off-the-shelf tool that answers from the documents you give it, one notebook per course. If the idea failed, I would have lost some time, not a budget.

## What went in

Only my own material: class notes, the case studies, and the code we ran in class. Before uploading, I removed everything meant for me alone: session timings, teaching cues, marking schemes, and anything related to exams. No textbook content went in. Then every number was rechecked against the actual code and data.

## Making it sound like the course

The personalisation was mostly a set of written instructions on how to answer:

- plain language first, formula second;
- use the cases the class already knows: the fraud desk at a payments company, a village census, a delivery start-up;
- say where in the course notes the answer comes from;
- when a question goes past the notes, say so clearly instead of improvising;
- a little dry humour, aimed at the material and never at the student.

## How it went

Access was limited to the students of the two courses, and each student's conversation stayed private to them. They leaned on it while building their end-of-course group projects, at hours when I was not available.

## What it can't do

It knows only what I gave it. Its voice is a milder version of mine.

## Next

A version anyone can use. Until then, the Learn by Playing section of this site is open to everyone.

::: {.signoff}
*Statistically Yours,*\
*Aritra*
:::
